transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-06-02 14:00 PDT
Duration: ~47 minutes
Attendees: Maya Patel (Redwood AE), Jonah Reed (Redwood SE), Liam Chen (Aurelia ML Eng), Priya Kapoor (Aurelia Infra), Dr. Marcus Hale (Aurelia Product)

Summary (auto): Weekly pilot check-in - focused on TTFT and streaming optimizations.

[00:00] Maya: okay hi everyone thanks for joining on time, Mia — sorry — Liam? good to see you all. we'll do a quick status and then jump into the numbers.
[00:18] Liam: hey Maya, thanks yeah we got the invite. we've been running the latest branch you pushed, ran the streaming patches last night.
[00:28] Jonah: great, thanks. I pulled the traces this morning; there's a few interesting spikes at the 1st-token path that we want to walk through.
[00:38] Priya: quick ask, can we confirm this call is okay to discuss logs? they're de-identified but still within our HIPAA policy.
[00:45] Maya: absolutely, Priya. we're covered by the NDA and the data in the traces is scrubbed per your ops team.
[00:52] Dr. Marcus: we also flagged the priority: TTFT under 80ms median is ideal for our clinician UI. 99th under 300ms is aspirational.
[01:06] Jonah: noted. so quick agenda: 1) quick recap of last week's baseline, 2) review streaming A run vs baseline, 3) kernel selection anomalies, 4) next experiments and network profiling.

[01:25] -- Baseline recap --
[01:26] Jonah: baseline (no streaming) median TTFT across our sample was ~145ms, 95th around 420ms. That was with sequence length mix we got from you last week - mostly 64/128 but a notable tail ~512 tokens for some summarization tasks.
[01:44] Liam: right yeah the summarizer pushes long seqs occasionally — those inflate our batching and the cache lookup times.
[01:51] Maya: and streaming run A we turned on smaller chunking (16 token chunks) and early-token path, correct?
[01:57] Jonah: yeah - streamingA used 16-token chunks, early-token path enabled, prefix KV caching off (we wanted to isolate chunking impact).
[02:08] Liam: what was the TTFT there?
[02:10] Jonah: median TTFT dropped to ~78ms for the 64/128 seqs, nice, but for the 512 seq tail we still saw 180-240ms medians — because kernel selection took a different path and there was more scheduling overhead.

[02:26] Priya: scheduling overhead meaning on the GPU or on our network?
[02:30] Jonah: mostly GPU task scheduling, and the runtime did a fallback to a less-optimized kernel for certain attention shapes at that sequence length. sometimes the kernel selector picks cuBLAS GEMM path vs our fused attention kernel based on sequence *and* batch dims.
[02:47] Liam: oh okay, so for long sequences it may be hitting a fallback that's slower. can we force the fused kernel?
[02:53] Jonah: we can suggest forcing it in the pilot but it's a trade — the fused kernel is faster for many shapes but for some shapes it actually regresses due to memory layout; we need the kernel traces to be sure.

[03:10] -- Observed noise and variance --
[03:11] Jonah: also saw variance around 1st-token latency correlating with network jitter in one AZ. When requests crossed AZ boundary we saw additional 20-40ms.
[03:22] Priya: that aligns with our infra notes — occasional cross-subnet egress on autoscaled workers during bursts. we'll run a constant-ping test this week.
[03:30] Maya: can you log that as a next step, Priya?
[03:33] Priya: yep.

[03:35] Dr. Marcus: curious — you mentioned prefix KV caching off for that run. what's the delta when we turn prefix caching on?
[03:43] Jonah: good question. in previous runs prefix caching reduced token generation latency by ~15-22% for repeated prompt prefixes (clinical templates). but it increased memory footprint and could hurt throughput in high-concurrency bursts.
[03:56] Liam: in our usage the clinician templates are reused heavily, so prefix caching could be a net win if memory isn't constrained.

[04:05] -- Kernel selection details --
[04:06] Jonah: I pulled specific kernel selection logs. For several 512-length requests the runtime chose a fallback GEMM kernel that had higher overhead due to extra memory copies. I can share the trace; it's attached to the pilot tracker but I'll also email it.
[04:18] Maya: please do. also include the quantization profile you used for the streaming run.
[04:23] Jonah: yes — streamingA used 8-bit quantization (dynamic int8) on the weights with per-channel scales. That saved inference cycles but changed numerical behavior slightly.
[04:34] Liam: we observed a very slight drop in rouge (about 0.6%) on long summarizations with int8 — not a dealbreaker but noted.

[04:44] Maya: has the team tried mixed-precision (fp16) paths for first-token vs int8 for subsequent tokens?
[04:50] Jonah: we did a hybrid in an internal run: fp16 for the first pass to keep high-fidelity, then int8 for streaming continuation. It reduced TTFT a bit, but complexity goes up and it's not currently a default in the hosted runtime.

[05:06] -- Streaming chunk size tradeoffs --
[05:07] Jonah: chunk size matters. 4-8 token chunks reduce per-chunk scheduling but increase per-token overhead; 16-32 token chunks hit sweet spot for our workload that has many 64-token responses. If you need sub-50ms TTFT median, 8 token chunks + prefix cache looked promising for your 64-token common case.
[05:29] Dr. Marcus: clinician UI wants feeling of instant start — they'd prefer faster first tokens over marginal throughput gains.
[05:36] Maya: that's an important product signal. we'll bias experiments towards TTFT.

[05:40] -- Cost implications --
[05:41] Liam: curious on cost delta — is aggressive streaming more expensive due to less batching?
[05:46] Jonah: possibly — smaller chunks can reduce batching efficiency, so per-token compute cost might go up. Redwood Optimize recommendations can show per-route cost delta; Maya will share numbers.
[05:56] Maya: yes I'll send a cost sketch for hosted vs dedicated with streaming enabled and with prefix caching toggled.

[06:02] -- Security and deployment mode discussion --
[06:03] Priya: one infrastructure constraint: any kernel-level trace uploads must be through our S3 that is in our VPC. we can't push traces to external endpoints.
[06:12] Jonah: understood — we'll share via your S3 pre-signed link or we can put logs into the private control plane for the Private deployment mock.
[06:20] Priya: also need to confirm KMS integration for keys, SSO SAML for user access, SOC2 report access — those were questions from compliance.
[06:29] Maya: we have SOC2 docs and KMS HSM details; I'll upload security pack to the shared drive. We support customer-managed KMS in Private and Dedicated plans.

[06:38] Dr. Marcus: timeline check — assuming the A/B runs look good and the infra test passes, when can we start a week-long pilot?
[06:46] Maya: if traces and sample are in by Friday and experiments finish over the weekend, we can propose a pilot start of Monday 2026-06-08. That gives us one week to validate.

[06:58] -- Deep-dive: specific trace sample walk --
[06:59] Jonah: I'll read one trace quickly: request id 0x9a2b - arrival to first kernel launch is 62ms, kernel exec 8ms, marshalling to network buffer 12ms, total TTFT 82ms. The outliers had arrival->launch spikes up to 130ms.
[07:18] Liam: arrival->launch spike correlates with our autoscaler spin-up events sometimes.
[07:22] Priya: we saw a CPU steal in one host at 03:12 UTC — that might explain it.

[07:28] Jonah: also a handful of requests went through a different rack with a slightly older GPU driver and that caused a fallback to a different kernel.
[07:37] Maya: worth standardizing drivers across pilot workers. Priya, can your team ensure driver parity?
[07:43] Priya: yes we'll coordinate; also we'll pin image versions for the pilot.

[07:47] -- Questions from Aurelia --
[07:48] Dr. Marcus: can Redwood guarantee that streaming won't change model outputs significantly (we need clinical consistency)?
[07:55] Jonah: streaming changes shouldn't alter model semantics — but quantization can. We'll run regression tests on your prompt set and report any deltas. If significant, we'll tune quantization or use mixed-precision.
[08:06] Liam: what's the rollback plan if we see quality regressions during pilot?
[08:10] Maya: we can pin to the non-quantized model for the time window, or switch to dedicated capacity with the chosen model variant; we also support canary traffic routing so you can route 10-20% to test path and 80-90% to baseline.

[08:23] -- Operational next steps recap --
[08:24] Maya: quick recap of action items: Jonah sends kernel traces and quant profile; Liam uploads 50k prompt sample; Priya schedules network ping and ensures driver parity; Maya sends cost sketch and SOC2 + KMS docs.
[08:38] Liam: added note — we'll also include a 99th-percentile sequence length breakdown per endpoint.

[08:45] Priya: one more infra ask — can we get a lightweight tracer that tags requests with AZ/rack so we can correlate?
[08:52] Jonah: yes we can enable a short header with hop metadata; we'll include that in the next traces.

[09:00] Dr. Marcus: okay sounds good. what's the expected deliverable timeline?
[09:04] Maya: kernel traces and cost sketch by Friday 2026-06-05; prompt sample by Thursday 2026-06-04; network session scheduled for next week (Jonah to propose times). Pilot start target 2026-06-08 if all looks green.

[09:20] -- Closing --
[09:21] Maya: anything else before we wrap?
[09:24] Liam: no, thanks. appreciate the fast turns.
[09:26] Priya: thanks all.
[09:27] Jonah: I'll make the trace attachments and add comments in the pilot tracker.
[09:31] Maya: great, I'll email the security pack and cost sketch. talk soon.
[09:34] Dr. Marcus: thanks everyone.

[09:37] (meeting ends)

Notes: occasional transcription errors in the recording (speaker tags may be slightly off). See attached pilot tracker for raw kernel logs and CSVs.
